A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INNAprop research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, GPT-2 pretraining, LoRA fine-tuning, and hyperparameter experiments in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DenseNet121 results, optimizer comparisons, and special-case parameter experiments.

M1.justification: The principal INNAprop update equations and Algorithms 1-2 are unchanged. Appendix Algorithms 3-4 replace fixed-K loops with an unspecified stopping criterion and revise return indexing, constituting limited changes to the stated procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, ImageNet, Food101, OpenWebText, and E2E with the same classification, pretraining, and fine-tuning tasks. Adding DenseNet121 changes model configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Sophia-G to GPT-2 Small pretraining comparisons in Figure 5 and INNA to GPT-2 Mini comparisons in Appendix F.5/Figure 19. These substantially broaden the language-model comparator set beyond AdamW to a second-order competitor and INNAprop's predecessor; citations to these methods in v1 were not equivalent experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds DenseNet121 evaluation and dedicated (alpha, beta) = (1,1) vision configurations. Tables 3-4 introduce Top-5 accuracy and steps-to-match-AdamW reporting. These extend evaluation within existing tasks; the retained experiments largely preserve their splits, schedules, and training durations.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds Figures 7-9 testing how the (1,1) special case compares with AdamW across CIFAR-10 and ImageNet training trajectories. Conversely, Figures 5-6 remove the (2,2) GPT-2 curves, reducing parameter-comparison evidence. Existing tuning heatmaps and the numerical-instability analysis remain.

E5.justification: New Table 3 describes ViT-B/32 results as coming from one run, whereas Figure 3 says three random seeds in both versions. This changes run-count reporting but leaves the actual repetition count unresolved. Existing eight-run CIFAR-10 and three-run LoRA reporting is retained; no new statistical testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds DenseNet121 accuracies of 86.19% for AdamW and 86.91% for INNAprop, ImageNet Top-5 results, and (1,1) trajectories. Figure 5 adds the Sophia-G comparison; Figure 19 shows INNA trailing AdamW and INNAprop. Table 4 newly quantifies steps to match AdamW, including 51,000 for GPT-2 Mini. The (2,2) GPT-2 results disappear. One ResNet18 comparison changes AdamW's 69.43 to 69.34, a value already reported elsewhere in v1.

T1.justification: The DIN/RMSprop dynamics, memory-saving derivations, alternative discretizations, and proof of equivalence to momentum-free Adam at (1,1) are retained. Appendix B.1's added curves provide empirical evidence rather than a new proof; equation renumbering does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain INNA combined with RMSprop scaling, second-order-inspired behavior with first-order-like computational requirements, and competitive performance against AdamW. The expanded abstract benchmark list and additional supporting results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Remark 3 newly interprets empirical similarity at (1,1) as suggesting that AdamW belongs to the INNAprop family, although the retained derivation establishes equivalence only without momentum. The conclusion also explicitly recommends (0.1,0.9) for language models. Existing generalization tradeoffs and resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G.4 changes reported GPT-2 pretraining hardware from eight to four A100 GPUs. Appendix F.5 specifies INNA's parameter pair, learning-rate search, and selected rate, and Section 3.3 adds a Sophia implementation reference. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 removes Castera et al. (2024) from the introduction and bibliography while retaining the 2021 INNA reference. Remark 3 expands the positioning relative to AdamW. The broader DIN, adaptive-optimization, and second-order-optimization context remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract enumerates benchmarks more explicitly, several passages are shortened, author emails are added, and acknowledgments are removed. Appendix F.5 is added, but the main narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the visual evidence: Table 1 is redesigned, Tables 2-4 summarize benchmark outcomes, and Figures 7-9 and 19 add comparisons. GPT-2 Figures 5-6 are redrawn with revised legends, curves, and axes. Other appendix figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The added Sophia-G and INNA comparisons strengthen empirical support beyond v1's AdamW comparisons, while the special-case experiments and Tables 2-4 make performance easier to assess. The net gain is limited: removing the (2,2) GPT-2 curves reduces sensitivity evidence, Table 3 introduces conflicting ViT run counts, and Remark 3 extends the AdamW interpretation beyond the unchanged momentum-free equivalence proof.
